metadata.note: The Duluth, Winnipeg and Pacific Railway (the 'Peg', DWP from 1960): a one-line railroad from Duluth through Virginia, Cook and Orr to Ranier and across the Rainy River to Fort Frances, Ontario, where its overnight train joined the Canadian Northern's for Winnipeg. Drawn from research/branches/duluth_winnipeg_and_pacific_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-11-03. Before this layer the map drew nothing for this company. Three features, one colour, because a feature has one geometry and the three stretches open in different years: Duluth - Virginia 1912, Virginia - Cook 1905 (earliest confirmed year, not an opening), Cook - Fort Frances 1908. All of it ends in 1961, when the last train ran overnight 30 June - 1 July. ONE COMPANY THROUGHOUT and so no Rule 4 split: the Duluth, Virginia and Rainy Lake (1901-05), the Duluth, Rainy Lake and Winnipeg (1905-09) and the DW&P (1909/1913-) were the same Canadian Northern subsidiary renamed, with the same managers and the same trains, and the 1918-23 passage of the Canadian Northern to the Canadian government changed the DW&P's parent, not its operator - the Feb 1952 Official Guide still names 'J. Conery, Superintendent D.W.&P. Ry., Virginia, Minn.'. CN train numbers and CN-leased locomotives do not make CN the operator of record.

metadata.freight_only: Rule 1 exclusions. (1) Everything after 30 June 1961: freight continued under the DW&P, CN and Wisconsin Central (31 Dec 2011) and the line is still CN's Rainy Subdivision today, but no segment is drawn past 1961 - hometownfocus confirms no passenger service by 1970. (2) The Virginia (DRL&W) - Rainy Junction - Virginia (DM&N) connection, about 3.8 mi: the Feb 1952 Official Guide's index reads 'Rainy Junction, Minn. - D. W. & P. Ry. (freight only)' and Fowler gives it no timetable letters at all, so it has no confirmable passenger year and is omitted entirely. (3) Falls Junction - International Falls: the rail there was the Minnesota, Dakota & Western, daggered freight-only in 1951, and the passenger link was an autobus - omitted. (4) The Northern Pacific trackage rights to Rices Point Yard are described by Wikipedia as a freight-interchange route; only the passenger trains' own approach to the Omaha depot is drawn, and its exact path is flagged as unresolved.
metadata.horsecar: Rule 5 not engaged: steam from the start (a logging railroad built from 1901). No animal traction.
metadata.rule_9: 2.4 mi of dwp-cook-fort-frances lies in Ontario, between the Rainy River bridge at Ranier and the CN yard at Fort Frances. This is Rule 9's southern-Canada exception - a US railroad's own trains reaching the border station they terminated at - and the research report recommends drawing it. Nothing beyond Fort Frances is drawn: the Canadian Northern / CN Winnipeg - Port Arthur main line the through train continued over is a Canadian railway and out of scope, including the stretch of it that dips back into Minnesota at Baudette and Warroad.
not_yet_sourced: Virginia - Cook start is OPEN: 1905 is the earliest year a source proves (1905 Official Guide listing via Fowler), not the year service began. The road was built from September 1901 for logging; whether it carried passengers before 1905 is unknown. Do not move this start earlier without evidence, and do not treat it as an opening date.

1912 vs 1913 for the Duluth - Virginia start: the first train ran 9 Dec 1912 'providing service ... on to Winnipeg' (MNopedia, american-rails), but MNopedia also says the 'dedicated passenger train' was introduced in 1913. The map draws 1912; either is defensible.

1908 vs 1909 for Cook - Ranier and the Rainy River bridge: 1908 rests on secondary accounts of the first train over the bridge (28 or 29 April 1908 - MNopedia's own body and timeline disagree on the day); the first primary evidence is the January 1909 Official Guide's station names (Orr as Pelican, Kinmount as Murlind), and Ranier carries Fowler letters only from 1914.

The Duluth terminal: which tracks DW&P passenger trains used from their own line into the Omaha (C&NW) depot at 200 S 5th Ave W is not established. Wikipedia gives 2.6 mi of Northern Pacific trackage rights to Rices Point Yard but in a freight context, and a 1954 photo caption mentions a DW&P 'elevated station' at Duluth. Needs a DW&P employee timetable or a Duluth terminal map; the first 3.9 mi of dwp-duluth-virginia is drawn on surviving terminal track as the best available guess.

The DW&P's own Virginia depot approach (600 Chestnut Street, built 1913) crossed Silver Lake on a trestle and is not drawn: the alignment is in neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap, so about 0.9 mi of the documented Duluth - Virginia mileage is missing from the drawn line.

1951 frequency: the Official Guide's equipment note makes the Winnipeg - Duluth buffet sleeper tri-weekly each way, but the OCR lost most of Table 189's times, so whether the train itself ran daily in 1951 is unknown. Every headway_min in this layer is an estimate of one train each way daily.
avg_speed_kmh: no complete run time was recovered for any era. 40 km/h is an unsourced estimate.

chicagorailfan.com prints a 1971 time column for Nos. 1/2 at Duluth that contradicts its own 'discontinued in 1961' note and every other source; treated as an error on that page, not as evidence of post-1961 service.

Out of scope but noted by the report as a possible missing layer in its own right: the Canadian Northern / CN Winnipeg - Port Arthur main line where it crosses Minnesota (Rainy River, Ont. - Baudette - Williams - Roosevelt - Warroad - Sprague, Man.). The Feb 1952 Guide's index puts CN passenger trains at Warroad, Minn. (Table 155). That is a Canadian railway inside the US - the reverse of Rule 9's case - and needs its own scope decision and report.

properties.line: Duluth, Winnipeg and Pacific: Duluth – Virginia
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not measured. No complete Duluth - Fort Frances run time was recovered: the Feb 1952 Official Guide's Table 189 times are mostly lost to OCR (a Duluth arrival '9 05 AM' is the one legible figure) and [CRF]'s 1942 entry gives only Duluth's own departure 7:15 PM and arrival 8:45 AM. 40 km/h is the order of magnitude for a once-daily all-stops train on this kind of single-track road, nothing more (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0), routed with opstrace.py: ways named 'CN Rainy Subdivision' / 'Rainy Subdivision' (the DW&P main line today), 'Duluth Winnipeg and Pacific Ry' (TIGER-named sidings and spurs), the abandoned 'DWP Trail' rail-trail and the OHM way whose operator is 'Duluth, Winnipeg and Pacific Railway' costed 1x; untagged track 1.25x; trails 3x; and any other named operator (DM&IR / CN Missabe and Iron Range subdivisions, BNSF/ex-GN, Erie Mining, Canadian Pacific, Mesabi Trail) 12x, so the trace could not stray onto the parallel DM&IR. Waypoints are the research report's via list, Nominatim-geocoded with every result's type checked (Cook came back as Cook County, Ash Lake as a lake and Kinmount as a creek - those were hand-pinned or dropped), chosen by opstrace's layered DP, then Douglas-Peucker (8 m) and trim_reversals. One continuous Duluth - Fort Frances trace was cut at Virginia and Cook so the three features share their junction vertices exactly.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap: 76.96 mi drawn against the documented 77.6 mi Duluth - Virginia (Fowler mileposts from Winnipeg: Duluth 379.6, Virginia 302.0; the Feb 1952 Official Guide gives Duluth 380.6, a 1 mi difference that is probably which depot was measured). NO STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: opstrace reported no approximated leg on this feature and no out-and-back spur; the longest single drawn step is a genuine 5.52 mi tangent north of Peary (47.3718,-92.5562 to 47.4484,-92.5897), checked by sampling 40 points along it, every one of them within 4 m of mapped track - Douglas-Peucker dropped the vertices because the real railroad is that straight. NOT DRAWN: the last 0.9 mi into the DW&P's own Virginia depot (600 Chestnut Street, 47.5231,-92.5411, built 1913, NRHP), which trains reached over a trestle across Silver Lake - that approach is lifted and appears in neither OSM nor OHM, so this feature stops where the main line passes west Virginia (47.5228,-92.5633), and that missing 0.9 mi is most of the gap between drawn and documented mileage. FOREIGN TRACK, drawn in this company's colour because these were its trains: the first 3.9 mi out of Duluth (46.7738,-92.1073 to 46.7285,-92.1763) runs on the surviving lakefront and Rices Point terminal track now tagged BNSF Railway, Canadian National or OHM 'Duluth and Iron Range Railroad' - the DW&P reached the Omaha (C&NW) depot at 200 S 5th Ave W over Northern Pacific trackage (Wikipedia puts those rights at 2.6 mi to Rices Point Yard, though in a freight context), and exactly which tracks its passenger trains used is NOT established (a 1954 caption mentions a DW&P 'elevated station' at Duluth), so the Duluth end is the least certain 4 mi of this layer. Within it, 0.21 mi (46.7401,-92.1536 to 46.7385,-92.1573) has no OSM way within 30 m and is carried by opstrace's 300 m end-connectors. A further 1.3 mi (46.7225,-92.1910 to 46.7011,-92.2226) is drawn on the Willard Munger State Trail and Clyde Connector Trail, which parallel the DW&P grade through Proctor where the DW&P's own grade is not mapped. 2.3 mi of the West Duluth - Nopeming climb is the abandoned grade itself as the 'DWP Trail'. ERA: the drawn alignment is the 1912 line as it survives today (still CN's Rainy Subdivision from Nopeming north); no later relocation is known on it, but the Duluth terminal trackage is today's, not demonstrably 1912's.

segments.note: Opened by the first train Duluth - Virginia on 9 December 1912, which MNopedia says gave service from Duluth over the Ranier bridge on to Winnipeg; american-rails dates the extension 'opened for service December 9, 1912'. MNopedia separately says a 'twice-daily, dedicated passenger train was introduced in 1913', so 1912 may have been mixed or first-train only - the map draws 1912 and the conflict is recorded in metadata.not_yet_sourced. Through overnight Duluth - Fort Frances - Winnipeg train over the DW&P's own railroad end to end. 1942: No. 1 dep Duluth 7:15 PM, No. 2 arr Duluth 8:45 AM [chicagorailfan]. Sept/Nov 1951: Official Guide Table 189 runs Winnipeg - Fort Frances 207.8 - Ranier - Duluth 380.6 with Nos. 1/2 and 19/20, and a CN equipment note 'Buffet Sleeping Car Winnipeg and Duluth (Nos. 1 and 2) 10-Section, 1 D.R.' tri-weekly each way - so this was rail, not a bus, in 1951. Fowler's letters a/b/c/d (1914, 1925, 1935 and 1956 timetables) independently confirm stops along this stretch in those years. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (one train each way daily); the 1951 OCR lost most times, so whether the train itself was daily in 1951 is not established - only the sleeper is known to be tri-weekly.
sources: Segment-level: the 9 Dec 1912 first train and the 1951 through service are cited for this stretch by name; the 1912-vs-1913 conflict and the estimated headway are flagged, not hidden.

segments.note: Last five years of the service. A Budd RDC-3 (D-301, delivered 1956) worked the Duluth - Fort Frances run with mail and express; 1956 averaged about five passengers a trip and 1959 lost some $160,000. Freight continued under the DW&P, then CN and Wisconsin Central (2011), and is deliberately not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE for one train each way daily; no 1956-61 timetable was read.

properties.line: Duluth, Winnipeg and Pacific: Virginia – Cook
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not measured - as for the Duluth - Virginia feature. Nothing was recovered for the 1905-08 logging-road era at all, where the real average was certainly lower.
properties.geometry_source: As dwp-duluth-virginia: the same single opstrace trace, cut at Virginia and Cook.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap: 26.08 mi against the documented 26.0 mi Virginia - Cook (Fowler: Virginia 302.0, Cook 276.0 from Winnipeg) - a 0.1 mi fit. NO STRAIGHT-LINE LEG and no out-and-back spur; every drawn mile sits within 30 m of a mapped way (16.0 mi CN Rainy Subdivision, 8.5 mi the OHM DW&P way, 1.6 mi TIGER 'Duluth Winnipeg and Pacific Ry' siding track). The south end is the main line west of Virginia (47.5228,-92.5633), not the Chestnut Street depot: see dwp-duluth-virginia for the un-drawn 0.9 mi Silver Lake trestle approach. ERA: this is the oldest part of the system (built from September 1901 as the Duluth, Virginia and Rainy Lake logging road) but what is drawn is the surviving alignment; no pre-1912 relocation is documented, and the 1905-era logging spurs and camp stops Fowler lists (Camp No. 5, Camp No. 6, Spur No. 12, Sand River, Putnam, Nelson) are main-line mileposts on this same stretch, not separate branches, so nothing extra is drawn for them. The longest drawn step is 4.67 mi (47.7909,-92.6419 to 47.8522,-92.6841) and samples along it stay within 5 m of mapped track, so it is a tangent and not an approximation.

segments.note: START IS THE EARLIEST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT AN OPENING. The 1905 Official Guide lists this line Virginia - Ashawa (Cook) with its logging-camp stops (Fowler's 'p' letter), and the Grand Rapids Herald-Review of 10 Feb 1906 calls Ashawa the road's 'present northern terminus'. The railroad was built from September 1901 for logging and whether it carried passengers before 1905 is NOT established - do not extend this start earlier without evidence, and do not read 1905 as the year service began. Operated by the Duluth, Virginia and Rainy Lake until Canadian Northern control and the Duluth, Rainy Lake and Winnipeg name in 1905; the 1905 purchase cannot be placed on either side of the one proven passenger year, so the whole feature is drawn under the DW&P name and colour rather than split. Mixed trains are likely for this era but the consist is not established; headway_min 1440 is a placeholder ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1905 rests on Fowler's 'p' = 1905 Official Guide listing for this exact stretch, corroborated by the Feb 1906 'present northern terminus' report; the open start is declared here and in metadata.not_yet_sourced.

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not measured - as for the Duluth - Virginia feature.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap: 67.62 mi against the documented 68.0 mi Cook - Fort Frances (Fowler: Cook 276.0, Ranier 210.8, Fort Frances 208.0 from Winnipeg). Split at Ranier the drawn line is 65.25 mi Cook - Ranier against 65.2 documented and 2.38 mi Ranier - Fort Frances against 2.8 documented; the 0.4 mi shortfall on the bridge leg is the Fort Frances station end, where the drawn line stops at the CN yard west of the Rainy River crossing (48.6138,-93.3959) rather than at a station platform, there being no station feature in OSM to aim at. NO STRAIGHT-LINE LEG and no out-and-back spur; 37.7 mi is drawn on the CN Rainy Subdivision, 3.1 mi on ways named plain 'Rainy Subdivision', 23.7 mi on the OHM DW&P way, 2.5 mi on TIGER 'Duluth Winnipeg and Pacific Ry' track, and the last 0.7 mi in Canada on the CN Sprague Subdivision and untagged yard track at Fort Frances. CANADA: 2.4 mi of this feature lies in Ontario (Rule 9's southern-Canada exception for a US railroad reaching its border terminal); nothing beyond Fort Frances - the Canadian Northern main line on to Winnipeg - is drawn. ERA: the drawn alignment is today's, which is the 1907-08 line; the Ranier rolling-lift bridge the trains crossed stood until it collapsed in 2024 (freight era, context only) and OSM still carries its alignment. The longest drawn step is 5.17 mi (48.4985,-93.3354 to 48.5733,-93.3401), within 4 m of mapped track throughout, and the next two (4.26 and 3.99 mi, Ray - Ericsburg) within 5 m: tangents, not approximations.
